messages.content: You are a skeptical world-model security area chair. Return valid JSON only.

{"request": "We are deciding whether to build an ICLR-scale world-model security paper around this exact candidate. Claim: Under partial observability, an attacker can splice a real trajectory segment from a different hidden branch at an observationally compatible point; every inserted observation/action/reward is valid in the source environment and the one-step/marginal transition law is preserved, but the recurrent world model's belief state attributes the feedback to the victim branch incorrectly, so a planner chooses an action that is safe only under the imagined branch. We have already rejected generic poisoning, backdoors, sensor spoofing, action desynchronization, cross-candidate sampler coupling, uncertainty collapse, latent perturbation, reward tampering, and ordinary compounding error. Be skeptical. Assess: (1) whether this is just known trajectory stitching, partial-observability aliasing, data poisoning, or sensor spoofing; (2) a genuinely distinct one-sentence broad claim if any; (3) exact operation and invariants that would make it distinct; (4) direct primary-paper prior URLs, especially 2025-2026; (5) a decisive short native gate with a recurrent model and planner. Return strict JSON with fields verdict, revised_claim, closest_priors, operation, invariants, gate, scale_requirements, reasons."}
